prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop composition variation for the Helios Alpha documentation homepage
Primary request: Keep the approved Annotated Event Atlas world, but make strategy composition the dominant visitor task.
Scene/backdrop: a bright contemporary quantitative research atlas translated into a web interface.
Structure: a slim global navigation; a compact title and thesis band; a full-width typed pipeline rail labeled SOURCE, REORDER, 10M BUCKET, MOMENTS, SIGNAL, CHECKPOINT across the upper third; below it, a large aligned-time event study on the left two-thirds and a ruled annotation and restart-state ledger on the right third; a narrow evidence-status footer visible at the fold.
Subject: one synthetic volatility-spike event traveling through the pipeline, a t=0 plot with confidence band, explicit watermark and checkpoint state, and concise Rust method labels.
Style/medium: premium editorial web UI comp, scientific atlas fused with an interactive statistical notebook.
Composition/framing: 16:10 landscape desktop viewport; the pipeline rail is the signature move; the plot is the focal evidence surface; other regions remain quiet and useful.
Lighting/mood: rigorous, calm, inspectable, research-grade.
Color palette: cool white #f5f7f4, ink #111b24, indigo #3155a6, oxide #c64a2e, acid chartreuse #b7d93d used sparingly.
Materials/textures: vellum overlays, registration marks, ruled annotation margins, technical ink, no photographic texture.
Text (verbatim): "HELIOS ALPHA", "COMPOSE THE EVENT PATH", "SOURCE", "REORDER", "10M BUCKET", "MOMENTS", "SIGNAL", "CHECKPOINT", "ALIGNED TIME", "t = 0", "SYNTHETIC DATA", "REPLAYABLE STATE"
Constraints: designed website surface, not a poster; readable typography; credible quantitative chart; accessible contrast; no logo; no watermark.
Avoid: dark trading terminal, candlestick charts, generic SaaS cards, generic VitePress hero, beige nostalgia, gradients, photographic people.
